summary: This study aims to systematically describe the form and function of novel melanopsin-based visual channels projecting to image-forming centers of the brain, specifically the dorsal lateral geniculate nucleus of the thalamus (dLGN) and the superior colliculus (SC). To achieve this, the study will characterize the morphology and physiological properties of intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs) that project to these areas using techniques such as patch clamp recording, intracellular dye filling, and confocal microscopy. The study will utilize a genetically modified mouse model with selective expression of GFP in ipRGCs to identify the cells of interest.
